'''Bahram Mashhoon''' ([[Persian language|Persian]]: بهرام مشحون, born 9 September 1947)  is an [[Iranian-American]] theoretical physicist who has contributed to the fields of special and general relativity. He is a Professor Emeritus of Physics in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Missouri]] in Columbia. He is known for formulating the [[Mashhoon effect]].

== Early life and education ==
Bahram Mashhoon was born in Tehran, Iran, on 9 September 1947.<ref name=":1" /> Bahram Mashhoon went to United States in 1966 to study physics. In 1969, he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Physics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], followed by a Ph.D. in Physics from [[Princeton University]] in 1972.<ref name=":1" /> His doctoral dissertation titled <nowiki>''</nowiki>''The Gravitational and Electromagnetic Interactions of a Black Hole''" was completed under the supervision of [[John Archibald Wheeler]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Hehl |first1=Friedrich W. |last2=Lämmerzahl |first2=Claus |date=2008-05-01 |title=Bahram Mashhoon's 60th birthday |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |language=en |volume=40 |issue=5 |pages=881–893 |doi=10.1007/s10714-007-0593-1 |bibcode=2008GReGr..40..881H |issn=1572-9532}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=296946}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
After completing his Ph.D., Mashhoon briefly served on the physics faculty of [[Aryamehr University|Arya-Mehr University]] (now [[Sharif University of Technology]]) in Tehran before returning to Princeton University as a research associate in 1973.<ref name=":1" /> He continued his research as a postdoctoral fellow and research associate within the relativity groups of Maryland and Utah from 1974 to 1978.<ref name=":1" /> Subsequently, he held positions as a lecturer and research fellow at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] from 1978 to 1980 before joining the gravitation group led by {{ill|Friedrich W. Hehl|de}} in Cologne, Germany, from 1980 to 1985.<ref name=":1" /> In 1985, he was appointed as an associate professor of physics at the University of Missouri-Columbia, where he held the position of professor of physics from 1995<ref name=":1" /> until his retirement in 2015.{{Citation needed|date=September 2025}}

After retirement, he returned to Tehran in 2017.{{Citation needed|date=September 2025}} He currently serves as an adjunct professor in the School of Astronomy of the [[Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences]] (IPM) in Tehran, Iran. He an adjunct professor of physics at the [[Sharif University of Technology]] in Tehran.{{Citation needed|date=September 2025}}

== Research ==
{{BLP primary sources|date=September 2025|section}}
He has made contributions to the theoretical exploration of various topics in gravitational physics including the quasinormal modes of black holes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ferrari |first1=Valeria |last2=Mashhoon |first2=Bahram |date=1984-04-16 |title=Oscillations of a Black Hole |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1361 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=52 |issue=16 |pages=1361–1364 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1361 |bibcode=1984PhRvL..52.1361F |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ferrari |first1=Valeria |last2=Mashhoon |first2=Bahram |date=1984-07-15 |title=New approach to the quasinormal modes of a black hole |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.30.295 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=30 |issue=2 |pages=295–304 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.30.295 |bibcode=1984PhRvD..30..295F |url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[gravitomagnetism]],<ref>{{Citation |last=Mashhoon |first=Bahram |title=Gravitoelectromagnetism: A Brief Review |date=2008-04-17 |arxiv=gr-qc/0311030}}</ref> tidal dynamics,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mashhoon |first=B. |date=1977-09-10 |title=Tidal radiation. |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1977ApJ...216..591M/abstract |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |language=en |volume=216 |pages=591–609 |doi=10.1086/155500 |bibcode=1977ApJ...216..591M |issn=0004-637X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mashhoon |first=B. |date=1978-07-10 |title=On tidal resonance. |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1978ApJ...223..285M/abstract |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |language=en |volume=223 |pages=285–298 |doi=10.1086/156262 |bibcode=1978ApJ...223..285M |issn=0004-637X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mashhoon |first1=Bahram |last2=Theiss |first2=Dietmar S. |date=1982-11-22 |title=Relativistic Tidal Forces and the Possibility of Measuring Them |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1542 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=49 |issue=21 |pages=1542–1545 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1542 |bibcode=1982PhRvL..49.1542M |url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[gravitational wave]]s, and cosmology.<ref name=":1"/>

In 1988, Mashhoon proposed that the intrinsic spin of a particle couples with the rotation of an observer in a specific way given by the spin-rotation Hamiltonian.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mashhoon |first=Bahram |date=1988-12-05 |title=Neutron interferometry in a rotating frame of reference |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2639 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=61 |issue=23 |pages=2639–2642 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2639 |pmid=10039184 |bibcode=1988PhRvL..61.2639M |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Its existence is due to the inertia of intrinsic spin. In [[interferometry]], the spin-rotation coupling in general appears in addition to the [[Sagnac effect]] that is due to the coupling of orbital angular momentum with rotation. The [[Mashhoon effect]] has been experimentally confirmed in neutron interferometry.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Danner |first1=Armin |last2=Demirel |first2=Bülent |last3=Kersten |first3=Wenzel |last4=Lemmel |first4=Hartmut |last5=Wagner |first5=Richard |last6=Sponar |first6=Stephan |last7=Hasegawa |first7=Yuji |date=2020-02-14 |title=Spin-rotation coupling observed in neutron interferometry |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41534-020-0254-8 |journal=npj Quantum Information |language=en |volume=6 |issue=1 |page=23 |doi=10.1038/s41534-020-0254-8  |doi-access=free|arxiv=1904.07085 |bibcode=2020npjQI...6...23D |issn=2056-6387}}</ref> The applications extend from the phenomenon of ''phase wrap-up'' in the [[Global Positioning System]] (GPS)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ashby |first=Neil |date=2003-01-28 |title=Relativity in the Global Positioning System |journal=Living Reviews in Relativity |language=en |volume=6 |issue=1 |article-number=1 |doi=10.12942/lrr-2003-1 |doi-access=free |issn=1433-8351 |pmc=5253894 |pmid=28163638 |bibcode=2003LRR.....6....1A }}</ref> to the spin-vorticity coupling in [[spintronics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nozaki |first1=Yukio |last2=Sukegawa |first2=Hiroaki |last3=Watanabe |first3=Shinichi |last4=Yunoki |first4=Seiji |last5=Horaguchi |first5=Taisuke |last6=Nakayama |first6=Hayato |last7=Yamanoi |first7=Kazuto |last8=Wen |first8=Zhenchao |last9=He |first9=Cong |last10=Song |first10=Jieyuan |last11=Ohkubo |first11=Tadakatsu |last12=Mitani |first12=Seiji |last13=Maezawa |first13=Kazuki |last14=Nishikawa |first14=Daichi |last15=Fujii |first15=Shun |date=2025-12-31 |title=Gyro-spintronic material science using vorticity gradient in solids |journal=Science and Technology of Advanced Materials |volume=26 |issue=1 |article-number=2428153 |doi=10.1080/14686996.2024.2428153 |issn=1468-6996 |pmc=11864018 |pmid=40012583}}</ref>

In 1993, Mashhoon introduced a nonlocal theory of accelerated systems in [[Minkowski space]]time.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mashhoon |first=Bahram |date=1993-05-01 |title=Nonlocal theory of accelerated observers |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.47.4498 |journal=Physical Review A |volume=47 |issue=5 |pages=4498–4501 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.47.4498 |pmid=9909459 |bibcode=1993PhRvA..47.4498M |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mashhoon |first=B. |date=2008 |title=Nonlocal special relativity |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/andp.200852009-1007 |journal=Annalen der Physik |language=en |volume=520 |issue=9–10 |pages=705–727 |doi=10.1002/andp.200852009-1007 |issn=1521-3889|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Subsequently, he pursued the development of a nonlocal theory of gravitation in collaboration with Friedrich W. Hehl, who suggested an indirect approach inspired by an analogy with the nonlocal electrodynamics of media.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hehl |first1=Friedrich W. |last2=Mashhoon |first2=Bahram |date=2009-03-26 |title=Formal framework for a nonlocal generalization of Einstein's theory of gravitation |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.79.064028 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=79 |issue=6 |article-number=064028 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.79.064028 |arxiv=0902.0560 |bibcode=2009PhRvD..79f4028H }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hehl |first1=Friedrich W. |last2=Mashhoon |first2=Bahram |date=2009-03-30 |title=Nonlocal gravity simulates dark matter |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269309002111 |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=673 |issue=4 |pages=279–282 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2009.02.033 |arxiv=0812.1059 |bibcode=2009PhLB..673..279H |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> A comprehensive account of this theory of nonlocal gravity is contained in Mashhoon's book {{harv|Mashhoon|2017}} and astrophysical and cosmological implications of this theory have been investigated in connection with [[dark matter]] and [[dark energy]].
